utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, everyone. Yes, Mr. Gaynor.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. I wanted to address one or two points arising out of the Defence motion concerning Mr. Zecevic's qualifications as an expert. The Defence after, Your Honours had ruled, put on record their reasons for their challenge, and in his submissions, Mr. Robinson referred to a couple of cases. He said there are a few cases at the Sierra Leone Tribunal and the ICTR where they have disqualified persons who may otherwise be considered to be expert because of their lack of impartiality. Now, these cases were not in fact referred to in the e-mail sent to us by Mr. Robinson on Sunday. And just to make sure that the record is absolutely clear, the -- neither of the two cases supports the contention made by the Defence. The first case is a decision of the 19th of June, 2008, which -- I'll read out the first part of the name of it to help identify what it is. The decision on the Defence application to exclude the evidence of proposed Prosecution expert witness, Corinne Dufka. Now, in that decision, which does not concern a scientific expert but, rather, a member of the Prosecutor in that Tribunal testifying about political and background matters, in that decision at paragraph 17, the Trial Chamber found that the person was not impartial but went on to say: "However, in the opinion of the Trial Chamber, this finding would not disqualify Ms. Dufka from testifying as an expert witness since concerns relating to the independence and impartiality of an expert witness are matters of weight, not admissibility." The Trial Chamber goes on at paragraph 26 to say that grounds 2 to 5 of the application are of academic interest only; and ground 2, to which it refers, is the impartiality question. The second decision cited by Mr. Robinson is, I believe, decision on a Defence motion for the appearance of an accused as an expert witness, filed in the Akayesu case on the 9th of March, 1998. Now, as the title of that decision suggests, one accused at the ICTR was hoping to call another accused at the ICTR as an expert witness in that case, and the Trial Chamber found that as the other accused, Nahimana, had been accused by the Tribunal for crimes related to those with which John Paul Akayesu is charged, and under similar counts, and for that reason they excluded the appearance of Nahimana as an expert in the trial of Akayesu. So neither of those decisions are remotely relevant to the position of Dr. Zecevic in this trial. Now, the final point I'd like to put on the record is that the proper vehicle, in our submission, for challenging the expertise of an expert or the relevance of his report is Rule 94 bis. And in Mr. Karadzic's Rule 94 bis filing of the 11th of May, 2009, he states that he does not challenge the fact that the witness is an expert and that his report is relevant. The singular word "report" in that filing appears to apply to all four reports listed in the Prosecution's 94 bis notification of the 26th of March, 2009, and there's no indication in that 94 bis filing of any challenge to the two reports challenged by Mr. Robinson in his e-mail which he sent on Sunday, on the very eve of the appearance of Dr. Zecevic, an expert witness whose appearance has been notified to the Defence many, many months ago. Now Mr. Tieger has some additional submissions to make with your leave, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, the submission is well-noted. Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I just wanted to raise a related systemic matter in connection with such notification that an issue will be raised. Incidentally by way of clarification, Mr. Gaynor noted that the cases to which Mr. Robinson referred had not been noted in the e-mail he sent, but it's also correct to say that the entire issue of partiality or impartiality had not been noted. But getting back to the systemic issue generally, it has been our understanding that the purpose of such e-mails was to advise the Trial Chamber and the Prosecution that an issue would be raised, and not an invitation, which we understood the Court would not welcome, for pleadings or submissions by e-mail. That understanding was shaken a bit when the Court effectively ruled on the e-mail objection without soliciting submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, let's stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Our decision was not triggered by that e-mail at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I -- and I was going to make that. I understood that, Your Honour, in that particular case. I just wanted to take the opportunity to mention that it continues to be our position that it's preferable for submissions to be made either in writing or orally in court and that the parties should be -- should take care to ensure that notification to the Chamber as an issue will be raised. Do not invite exchanges that are better held in formal pleadings or orally in court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Your points must have been taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Excuse me, Mr. President. I don't want to belabour this much and we're open to whatever guidance the Chamber wants to give us on how to make our submissions. In general, if it's an issue of evidentiary matter or exclusions of evidence or objections to evidence, we try to do them orally, and otherwise we do them in writing. But if you have any other guidance you want to give us, we're ready to follow that. With respect to the points that Mr. Gaynor made, if I could just point out that in our notice, at paragraph 3, we said Dr. Karadzic respectfully provides notice that he does not accept the expert witness statements and/or reports and that he wishes to cross-examine the expert. And he doesn't challenge the fact that the witness is an expert but reserves the right to object at trial to opinions offered outside the expertise of the witness. Second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's leave the matter there. We have admitted that report already. So it's all -- leave the matter as it is. And let's deal with it when it arises again. Let's bring in the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Good morning, Doctor. Please make yourself comfortable.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency. Good morning to everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will have to be making pauses between questions and answers, then, because many things are not recorded in the transcript. Is it correct that in chapter 8 of your report from 2007 you looked at the probable dispersion of modified air bombs and cited as the reason the simple sum of some effects on the bomb, for example such as mass, the change of impulse, and other things? Would you like me to call up that part of your report?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. And these elements, are they usually not taken into account when you calculate the firing elements?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. If you take into account the firing tables, and in accordance with military firing standards, they are taken into account.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please pause between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I'm going to repeat my answer. All these elements are taken into account while firing when using military systems that are used according to military standards and for which there are firing tables. But I would like to emphasise: No unguided rocket, artillery, or mortar system can hit a pinpoint target. It can only fire at an area of a certain dimension or certain size that is measured in scores of metres or kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In paragraph 13 of the same report, I will call it up if necessary, you said: "The military technical institute probably drafted the basic firing tables thanks to which it was possible to calculate the range at a certain angle of elevation and make possible corrections of the range due to certain changes of the air temperature. It's possible that corrections were made in change of target due to wind, but there were no conditions in order to be able to ascertain the actual vector of the wind speed." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We did not have the original or the translation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I could not comment on this last sentence of yours, but it's a fact that the basic firing tables do not provide for the military use of that system. They are only used in the testing stages in order to be able to use it in wartime by soldiers for military purposes, and not by qualified personnel, for example, personnel of the military technical institute or the military training institute. It is necessary to draft the complete firing tables in order to draft these firing tables, before that you would need to carry out a series of experimental testing, a lot of testing, in order to be able to carry out gradual defining of the firing tables. Once -- the drafting of the firing tables is a very complex task. It requires expert, professional staff, material resources, if you want to use that particular ammunition for military uses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Put a pause. Slow down. These are very technical issues and it's very difficult for us to follow. So we have to come back to the transcript later on at a later stage, particularly so that for that reason the transcript should reflect the real conversation as much as possible. Please slow down. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We do need to call up the 65 ter 08347, please. 08347. And the first -- can we look at page 1 so that Mr. Zecevic can identify the document. And then can we look at 77 in the Serbian and 84 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And while we are waiting, Mr. Zecevic, let me ask you this: Do you know what testing was actually carried out?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, if on the basis of remnants of rocket projectiles that were found in Sarajevo you establish that there are different series of rocket engines and if on the basis of available information you established that rocket engines of 127 millimetres were used, 122 millimetres were used, and if you establish that 128-millimetre K13 rocket engines were used, if we know that Yugoslavia, the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, did not manufacture the grad rocket engines and the Pretis factory was developing that rocket system and did not complete it, that means that in no case could anyone have completed that system because the fuel -- rocket fuel manufacture was done in Slobodan Princip Seljo factory in Vitez, which is the main criteria in order to define the energetic parameters of such a system, meaning that it was not possible for any person involved in ammunition or weapons design. It's clear that in 1994, in January, and in 1995, this usual procedure of testing could not have been completed, procedure of development and introduction into the regular weapons system of a new rocket -assisted system. And then you could not really predict not the area but the zone where these rocket systems could be active.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could Mr. Karadzic please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. The interpreters couldn't hear your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Vitez. Was this rocket fuel from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, which rockets? Three types of rocket engines were used. Which ones?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was the fuel in any of the three rockets that you mention, as being in possession of the Army of Republika Srpska, come from Vitez?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Organj 128-millimetre rocket fuel was from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And how did we obtain that, Mr. Zecevic, when Vitez was under the control of the Army of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Very simply, Mr. Karadzic, because these were rocket engines that were manufactured before the war, because the Army of Republika Srpska and the Army of Yugoslavia had rocket systems of the Organj type.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you don't know what was produced but you just, by analogy, conclude that they already had them; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, there is the UPR 2 rule books. This is the administration for production and development and procurement of ammunition of the General Staff of the Yugoslav People's Army, where it is clearly defined which procedure is used in order to decide if a system would be developed, when this decision is adopted, that some weapon system would be developed. Then there is a clearly defined procedure whereby the development is carried out. It sets who will manufacture and who will control the production process, how the testing will be carried out, how will somebody decide whether this system will be introduced into the weapons system or not. So this book of rules is used by the armed forces of Bosnia-Herzegovina as well. It was also used by the Yugoslav People's Army and probably by the Army of Republika Srpska, because this was a main basic system of an ordered military formation and an ordered state at that point in time. Without it, it was not possible to introduce any armed system and it was not possible to allow to introduce any armed system into the military which was not developed according to that rule book. In the event of the import of any kind of new weapons system, the rule book specifically stated what the procedure was. So there were all procedures clearly laid down about what had to be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you still don't know what was actually done, but you are making a conclusion on the basis of familiarity with this particular rule book; is that correct or not? We don't need to lecture any more. Is it correct that you don't know but you just conclude what was done and what was tested on the basis of analogies that you draw from being familiar with the book of rules? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Mr. Karadzic. The rule books.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's leave the rule book aside, please, do you know what was carried out, out of the technical testing? Do you know or not?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you put a general question to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's not a global question. For these rockets, 128, grad 13, 122 rockets, and for this new use, do you know what was done and what was actually not done? Without any analogies. Do you know what was actually done?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, based on the documents left behind by Mr. Radomir Ecimovic in the Pretis factory, I could read what was supposed to have been done. I had some of his telegrams and I was able to read them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about Radomir Ecimovic, did he leave all of his papers in Pretis?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I really am not authorised to give you such an answer. I did not have access to all the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did the Serbs take all the machines, the presses, when they left and handed over Vogosca to the federation?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot give you a precise answer, but they took most of the machines, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And of course they then could have taken away the papers too; they were lighter than the machinery, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, what do you mean when you say "papers"?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The same thing that you mean when you say "papers." You mentioned the papers. But let's leave that aside. How do you know that these engines, grad -- Organj 128 and grad 13, were not -- that special firing tables were not developed for these particular systems?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't make firing tables for these particular weapons but you make them for the systems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How do you know that then the tables were not made for the systems?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there must be a standard, Mr. Karadzic, for the fuel that is used in a specific rocket engine. And the fuel standard for the grad rocket was not developed at that time. The K13 rocket was imported from the Soviet Union; it was some 30 years old or more. The standard for the rocket fuel for the Organj system as applied in the Organj rocket system did exist, but if that rocket system and the rocket engines of the Organj type were supposed to be used in a system with three or four rocket engines, it would need to be tested as a whole using the three or four rocket engines and then only on the basis of that could you make the firing tables, not individually looking at the performance of a single rocket engine but looking at the ballistics performance of three or four rocket engines taking into account of this rocket-assisted system that would be used. It's a clear procedure. Every armed system must have its own characteristics, its performance, its description. Somebody has to stand by that, they have to sign that and guarantee that the system would not kill its own soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a five-minute break. --- Break taken at 9.27 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, do we agree that while products were being imported, each of the products were tested and were given some sort of an ID card?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In terms of the clear procedures, within the PRF, each product had to meet the criteria set out in UPRF 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever come across anything like that or did you find any documents that during one and the same incident, different series of rocket engines were as a matter of fact used?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't confirm that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Why did you refuse to comment on the following sentence? It is possible that corrections were made to the range because of the wind, but there were no conditions to determine the real wind velocity vector.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Excuse me. Could I ask Dr. Karadzic to clarify where or when the witness refused to comment on that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. I was about to ask him that question. Could you clarify, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that was at page 10. That was when I read back everything. When I quoted, Mr. Zecevic said the last sentence: "I will not comment or I cannot comment." It's probably at page 10. Today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why did you refuse to comment?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I just ask you where I said that in my analysis, phrased like that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 91 of your report.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I have a look, please?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] English 99, Serbian 91, those are the references. Can we please have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The last paragraph. The last sentence. It is possible that changes were made to the range because of the wind, but there were no conditions to establish the real wind velocity factor.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I explain that?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why will you not comment on that last sentence? That's what I want to know, the reason.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm asking you again, may I explain what I mean by that? Mr. President, may I?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. For the record, it's on pages 6, lines 12. Mr. Karadzic's question appears from the previous page and then the witness said I could not comment on this last sentence of yours. So if you could proceed to answer, Dr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The matter is actually really simple. When you produce firing tables, you make assumptions about the influence of the wind, how it may affect the range or the direction of a projectile. In a real time, real weather conditions, whenever there is firing, if you're a serious unit you need to have meteorological parameters; you need to measure the temperature, the air pressure, the wind velocity; you need to examine the atmosphere, so to speak, in order to have accurate firing. So my sentence, the one that we are talking about, refers to my own estimate for the following: At that point in time, within the VRS, there was no system in place to measure these atmospheric parameters and there was no capability of assessing objectively the wind velocity in a certain layer of the atmosphere in order to be able to adjust their firing accordingly. So that is what I when I wrote that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. So you don't know. You simply assume that the VRS didn't have that; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know what the JNA had before the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Another question. One last question about this. Do you have any proof indicating that no testings were carried out? Or, rather, which testings -- which tests were carried out and which weren't of these performances?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the whole world is trying to get the so-called standardisation system to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's leave the world alone for the time being and any other system. What about the system we're talking about? Do you have any proof that these systems weren't tested and that the performance tests were not run in relation to these?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not offer any material proof. All I can give you is my analysis as an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: May I add something?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you wish to do so, please, but do corroborate by all means.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was possible to run tests only in the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia but not in Bosnia-Herzegovina. There were no conditions there for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You say in your report you're trying to prove that in most of the incidents in Sarajevo aerosol bombs were used; is that right, sir?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Just the incidents that I looked into.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you enumerate those, please?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A total of 15 such incidents that I looked into, that I studied. One, Sarajevo TV, the Sarajevo TV building.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: An aerosol bomb; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Number 2, Zajko Street. Number 3 -- well, actually - one, two, three, four - about five incidents altogether, I believe, or six, in the Hrasnica area. Another incident near the Elektroprivreda building in Sarajevo, an incident when a projectile landed on top of a building. And this was the lung disease institute or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. We'll go back to that later on. Why does no one else apart from you make any mention of aerosol bombs? No one apart from you. The UN don't mention that in any of their reports.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, perhaps you should address the question to the UN directly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Perhaps we should try and simplify the technological aspects of this situation. You say that the casings for these air bombs had aerosol fillings, aerosol charges; right? That's what you're suggesting?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are you claiming that 90 kilograms of explosive was taken out, and then how many litres exactly of aerosol were poured into its place?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never said that hard, solid explosive was taken out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We have an aircraft bomb. In order for it to be shattered into fragments of a certain number of kilograms, 7.000, 5 grams, what would be the weight of that projectile? Where it is splintered into 7.000 fragments, each 5 grams each, what would be the weight of that projectile?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said the bodies of these air bombs were used.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mean the casings?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Were they eventually emptied at some point by anyone, emptied of that their original charge? That I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Instead of these 90 kilograms of TNT, what was within the warhead?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a hollow within the warhead and what we find there is a primary explosive charge, and that's what needs to be there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How much does it weigh?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In case of a -- in case of an FAP air bomb 275, it's based on aerosol, I would say between 5 and 10 kilos of solid explosive. The rest is filled with liquid gas, propylene oxide, ethylene oxide, pyropylene, and other types of liquid gas, in addition to the primary explosive charge which is triggered by a fuse, the objective being to destroy the metal structure and create the conditions for the liquid gas to start evaporating, which it starts doing as soon as 37 degrees Celsius temperature has been reached. And then we have a secondary charge. And the purpose of that is to activate the secondary mixture of aerosol. That is the concept on which the aerosol system, as we call it, is based.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Are you trying to tell us the following: We have these ten kilos of explosive, it produces a total of 7.000 fragments or shrapnel, 5 grams each, or more?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what you're suggesting, Mr. Karadzic. I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. Well, then you go ahead and tell us. You have 10 kilograms of explosive within that casing. And then this is shattered into a total of 7.000 splinters or fragments. What about a 10-kilogram charge, how many splinters would that produce?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, that is entirely irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There is something wrong with the transcript. Just a minute, please. My question: We have 90 kilograms of explosive. This produces 7.000 pieces of shrapnel or fragments. What about 10 kilograms of explosives? How many pieces of shrapnel would 10 kilograms produce, and how much would each of these fragments weigh?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, if you look at an air bomb with a solid explosive charge, it has two functions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This -- you're lecturing us.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not lecturing you. You're asking me a question which is unclear. An air-fuel bomb has the following primary task: It needs to produce a blast effect. The fragmentation effect is a secondary one; it's unimportant. The only objective being to destroy a certain structure and to get the aerosol or air fuel to start blending with the surrounding air.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Air fuel or aerosol doesn't actually explode before it leaves the casing, does it? As soon as it starts blending with the surrounding air, that's when it explodes; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that correction would seem to be a posit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What about the explosion of the hard casing? The effect needs to be produced by a solid explosive, say up to 10 kilograms, within the air fuel. So what effect is wrought on the casing by the 10-kilogram explosive and how many fragments would that produce and how much would with each of those fragments weigh, if we had 10 kilograms of this solid explosive?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would it be more or less than 7.000?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be less.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Because the fragments are bigger?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you locate those fragments?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I did not study these cases myself. I drew up an analysis based on a photo file and based on reports carried out by the relevant bodies, relevant investigative bodies. With the exception of the TV building incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's hold on to that example the TV building and then we will go back to how many fragments are produced by a 10-kilogram explosive mass as opposed to the 90 kilogram one. But let's go back to the TV building.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 08347, please. 65 ter 08347. This is the same document. 1D3282.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You say that an air-fuel bomb exploded on top of the TV building and there were some scattering or fragmentation, some shrapnel flying around; right?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 003 -- that's page 4 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this an image from your report? The shape and appearance of shrapnel found in Studio C of the TV building?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You did this for the investigating magistrate, you and two other colleagues of yours; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about these pieces of shrapnel? Do they look typical of an explosion created by an explosive of the classical type?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The shape is sabre like and they're actually quite large. The bits of shrapnel are quite large, which shows you that the effect of the detonation was not primarily the fragmentation of the projectile itself.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 08347, next one up, please. The page is 103 in the Serbian and 114 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If you look at these rocket launcher barrels and you see the damage, would that appear to have been caused by shrapnel, by bomb fragmentation?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A classic explosive being used; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3283 is the next document. Thank you. 1D3283, a single one will do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: What about the shapes of these bits of shrapnel? And then if you look at the damage caused on the left-hand side --

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry I interrupted you. You keep forgetting one thing. It was 300 by 100 millimetres. That would have been the dimensions. And it's roughly this size that I'm showing to you. And the calibre here is 122 millimetres, which means that the gash, the slash caused by the bits of shrapnel, should be about 90 millimetres. Bearing that in mind, this wasn't a full-on penetration but, rather, this was caused by the kinetic energy produced by the penetration of the bits of shrapnel. And therefore we can't effectively compare the photograph on the right and the effects of the explosion, the damage, on the left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, we see pictures of these bits of shrapnel here on the left-hand side. We see the traces of the damage, a classic bomb with a classic charge, and the type of damage that it caused to the barrels of this multiple rocket launcher. How do you explain what you just said a minute ago, that there is no comparison that is possible?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the effects in both cases. If we are talking about the air-fuel bomb or if we are talking about the fragmentation bomb carrying a solid explosive charge, there will always be some splintering, some fragmentation. The effects of the splintering process are secondary if we talk about an air-fuel bomb. If we talk about a classic air bomb with a solid explosive charge, that's a different thing altogether. And everybody knows that. It's common knowledge. It's easy enough to check. You don't need to talk to me necessarily. You can talk to anyone. Take any book on military ballistics and terminal ballistics and it's right there. Easy for anyone to track down that type of information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's time to take five-minutes' break. --- Break taken at 9.55 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do we agree, Mr. Zecevic, that the right-hand side of the photograph depicts the fragments that were found in the TV building in Studio C; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I cannot look at my own report, I cannot confirm that. This is a black and white photograph, and the quality is very poor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A few moments ago we asked for that. 65 ter 1D3282 actually, page 4. Is this a page from your report?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have the photograph back again now, 1D3283.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see that it's the same photograph from your report?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If we agree that these are 128-millimetre barrels, how big are these fragment traces? 5, 7, 220 centimetres; right? Or 50, 70, 200 millimetres; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are barrels of 122 millimetres from a multiple rocket launcher. Further on, the fragments were created when a laser-guided air bomb exploded, a GBU-39. The effects of fragmentation are quite different from the effects when it hits the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: How big are these fragments that they found for you at the TV centre? Did you collect them or did they bring them to you?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not collect them. It was a group of the Ministry of the Interior that did. I did not have that kind of authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the size of these fragments found at the TV station? What is the range?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you have that other page recalled? It happened 16 years ago and I didn't even have an opportunity to refresh my memory because I was in prison.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this photograph please be admitted so we don't have to call it back again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1091, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D3282, could we have that again, page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 5? Four.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Look at the subtitle here -- or, rather, the subheading. It says here that the biggest fragments found were 100 by 300 by 7 millimetres, while the rest were considerably smaller. What does this look like to you? Was this done by 10 or 90 kilograms of explosive?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I cannot give an answer to that question because it would be imprecise. These dimensions are these dimensions that you see here now. See? These dimensions. That's the shrapnel. 300 by 100, and the thickness is 7 millimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's the biggest one and all the rest are smaller?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, smaller. It can be 150 by 100 or whatever. No one actually measured them, so we can just speculate. And I do not wish to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Hrasnica. Let us look at the incident in Aleksa Santica Street, number 50, in Hrasnica. The investigation authorities determined that the shell came from the north and then the bomb ricochetted into another street. Is -- was that the finding of the police of Sarajevo? Can we have the document, to make it easier for you?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 08347. Please identify the first page first, and then page 161 in English, 139 in Serbian. 08347 is the 65 ter number. And now the Serbian page is fine. The English should be 161. 161. You had 157 there. In e-court. In e-court, 161.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are these the findings of the police? Or, rather, can you explain this photograph to us? The two photographs, rather, on the right-hand side.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can. Very simply. The projectile flew in, grazed the house. You can see that on the first photograph, that part of the house was destroyed. The projectile went on because its mass was enormous, about 300 or 400 kilograms, so it went on and ultimately hit the water tap there; right? And then in my view it hit the ground, destroyed the water pipes. Water and fuel, aerosol, were mixed, and that can be seen very easily because the effects of aerosol are very poor in the rain and in humid conditions, generally speaking, so there was no explosion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. You did not agree -- actually, look at the first photograph. What we see in the forefront is a fence that was torn down, and we see soil, piles of soil. The projectile flew in - that's what the police established - grazed the corner of the house, and then, on the left-hand side, we see the destroyed fence and it hit the ground and then it ricochetted. You did not accept that; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not because it's impossible for a ricochet to take place at a 90-degree angle. Do you understand what I'm saying?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where do you see 90 degrees here?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Look at the position where they said that the projectile flew. The subsequent report said that it was exactly 90 degrees in relation to the house and in relation to the trajectory, the direction from where the bomb arrived.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did it ricochet off the house or the ground, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, the house has nothing to do with it whatsoever if there is this pressure on the ground. That is to say, the projectile hit the ground. And before that, it had grazed the house. Once it had hit the ground, there is no possibility, ever, theoretically, for a projectile once it hits the grounds that it can turn at a 90-degree angle. It can just go further up a bit to the left or right, but this is classical mechanics.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Please look at the left-hand photograph. The police established that where the defence [as interpreted] was torn down, that is where the projectile arrived and the engines were left, and then it ricochetted off the ground, not the house, so the angle of descent of this projectile was not 90 degrees.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahhh [phoen].

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Could I ask that the accused could show the police report or show the source of all this information to the witness if he's asking the witness to comment as to whether he agrees with the assertions set out in the police report or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, let us do that, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You had a look at this police report, didn't you, Mr. Zecevic, and you disagreed with it and you said that this ricochet was impossible; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, on page 135 of this report of mine, it says, investigators' opinion, and it reads as follows: "The investigators state that this projectile first hit the house at Aleksa Satica, number 50, went through the corner of the house, hit the ground. The rocket motors detached, the projectile ricochetted and continued flying towards the street Bunicki Potok 233 and 231, remains of 122-millimetre grad rocket motors were found. It was estimated that the projectile came from the north on the basis of the damage on the house." And I, when I marked the point of impact on the ground, on a map, and also the positions of the two houses for which the investigators say that are the result of one the same projectile, I determined that the positions of the houses were at an angle of 90 degrees in relation to the trajectory, the direction from which the projectile had come from. That is impossible. There is not a single guided projectile that can, over a short time span, in a small area, make a 90 per cent -- 90-degree manoeuvre, let alone an unguided projectile.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So when we look at this picture, let us agree temporarily that a ricochet is impossible if you determined the angle of descent of the projectile in the Aleksa Santica street on that condition. So you established that the bearing can be determined in relation to the house, the accuracy is plus/minus 5 degrees; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is what my report says.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that you determined the incoming azimuth only to be able to increase the number of projectiles that had been fired and to prove that this one had been impossible?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, that is so unprofessional, but you are entitled to that. The direction from which the projectile came and the angle of impact are determined very easily in this case. The point where the house was damaged and the point of impact on the ground when the projectile -- where the projectile was found, if you link the two up, it is going to be so easy for you to determine the direction from which the projectile came, as well as the angle of descent. There is no dilemma there whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the last part of the sentence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Could you both of you slow down. The interpreter couldn't hear your last sentence, Mr. Zecevic. Did you say something after "There is no dilemma there whatsoever"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] After that, I said thank you for that, and now we are going to go precisely along those lines. Can we now have 65 ter, the very same document, actually, page 140. And in English it is 163.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: I'd just like to note for the record that the accused was quoting from a police report. He was putting to the accused -- he was putting to the witness certain assertions from the police report. The accused was then directed to show the police report to the witness and he did not do so. I just want to note that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But he -- the witness himself referred to the investigators' opinion that appears in his report.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Yes, but -- very well, but if Dr. Karadzic is going to expressly quote from a report that he appears to be holding, I think in fairness that should be shown to the witness so the witness can agree or disagree with the assertions that are made from a report that Dr. Karadzic may be holding and that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I think we can move on. The witness was happy with his reference, his citation he cited in his report. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you mark on this photograph the approximate direction and the approximate point of impact of the projectile?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This photograph was dealt with by the investigators. On this photograph and in this text, I only wished to demonstrate that the point of impact of the projectile at the corner of the house was about 20 metres away from its point of impact on the ground, and that the system involved solid -- had there been solid explosive on this white wall, there would have been hundreds of traces from the explosion of that kind of air bomb; whereas on this wall we cannot see a single trace of fragmentation. That was the point of what I wrote there, which clearly indicates that the basic type of projectile is something different. It is not a high-explosive warhead, that is to say, warhead with a fragmentation effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Who drew these yellow arrows?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yellow arrows? Sorry. I drew the yellow arrows on the basis of direct insight on the very spot. Because as I looked at the investigators' reports, I visited each and every location, I interviewed all the persons who were there at the time, if they had survived or if they hadn't moved out, and I tried to experience this in reality, what is written in the investigators' report, that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: When did you do that, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, it says up here, January 2007, when I was entrusted with this task of compiling this analysis.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about the police investigators, when did they carry out their investigation?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it is all written there. You can see it there. I cannot tell you exactly now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, there is no dispute there that it did not explode on this house. In order for it to be able to explode, it had to hit the house with a fuse; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. If the diameter is 320 millimetres or 350 millimetres, it could have hit it with the lateral part of the projectile, because it has an enormous mass of 350 to 400 kilograms. I cannot say exactly, but it's a ballpark figure. Say it's -- it weighs 220 or 230 kilograms, the bomb itself, and then there are four rocket motors, say each one of them is about 25 kilometres -- kilograms, that would mean 75 kilograms, then that 300 kilograms, and then everything else that it has to be fitted with, we can talk about 350 to 400 kilograms safely. That kind of mass, Mr. Karadzic, that is flying at the speed of 100 metres per second, and 100 metres per second is about 500 kilometres per hour, Mr. Karadzic, that is a system that destroys everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So if it hit laterally, it could not have been activated; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it all depends. Had it involved a laser system, then probably that would have been the case. But in this case it was not a laser system. It was a forward fuse, and non-guided. So it was not activated when it hit the building, but when it hit the water tap, that is when water surged out of the water pipe and that is what affected the aerosol.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is your assertion that the projectile hit where the tip of the arrow is?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that where it exploded?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the ground, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's time to have a half an hour break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I'd like to -- please take a look at the screen, at the bottom left photo. 12 or 13 years after the incident, you established that a shell had grazed the house and then fell on the ground and landed where the arrow is pointing on the ground; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please now take a look on the left-hand side of this photo, at the edge. Is that a fence?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now have, again, page 140 of this document, that's in B/C/S. And 162 in English. Page 139 in Serbian, 161 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at this photograph on the left-hand side. Is this a photo that was made by the police at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, probably, because that was the photo that I was given.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, can you see the fence there that is actually on the ground?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you believe that closer to the house, where you indicated that the bomb must have landed and where some people are standing, that the police had not seen that effect on the ground and fragments and so on of the shell but, rather, indicated the area around the fence where the stabiliser or the rocket motors were found?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a -- let's collapse the English page and zoom on the B/C/S version. We can zoom in further on the left photo. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So here we see the fence that we had seen a moment ago, and this is the house that was grazed by the shell. Now, you indicated with an arrow the point of impact where the shell landed, and that's approximately where these two men are standing in the photo here?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, where, then?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's simple. Each photo is an intuitive sense or impression of the individual who analyses it, and it also depends on the lens that you use to make a photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please indicate on this photo here the yellow arrow that you indicated on the other photo and tell us where it was that the shell landed. Show us.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't do it on this photo. Can you please pull up my photograph?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, let me help you. You said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's up -- can we upload the next page as well? Let's zoom out first. Collapse the English page. No, no, no, we -- this is the right -- the right page is page what?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Here. Now, is it possible to keep this photo on the right-hand side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And my question is whether we can upload the next page of B/C/S on the left side.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation] --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No, no, previous - I'll answer - previous page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now can we have page 139 on the left part of the screen, the split screen?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told it's possible. Yes. And we can zoom in each page, the left photo on the left side and the -- yes. We can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now, Mr. Zecevic, 12 or 13 years after the incident, you established that the shell impacted the ground where you pointed it; whereas the police, at the time of the incident, established that the shell had ricochetted there, left or ejected its motors, rocket motors there, and then continued on its path. Now, how is it possible and what do you base your assertion on that that -- that this is in fact the point of impact?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Previous translation continued]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, your answer was not reflected in the transcript. What did you say?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, the question is not fully reflected either.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was -- I was unable to actually answer the question because I realised that the interpreters were trying to catch up. I would just like to read what it is that I stated there. The arrow that I put there was based on my conversation with the people who lived in that house and who showed me the place or the point of impact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And the police showed you this photograph; correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I received this data from the Prosecutor's Office.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, let us now see, if we were to put -- indicate the point -- the point of impact, and we connected it to where it is claimed that the house was hit or grazed, we would get the azimuth north; correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, Mr. Karadzic, on the left-hand side of the photograph, the point of impact is not indicated at all. All I see here is a marking saying "1" and the point where this projectile grazed or went through the building. And this photograph was made with a wide-angle lens, and it is not quite precise. The photo is a little bit skewed. My photograph was made from a different angle, so you can't really draw conclusions and parallels between the two.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you show the right photo on the left side. We can scroll to the right. Who made that yellow line, Mr. Zecevic? Was it you? That yellow line.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is that the same house, Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now get the left-hand side of the page again on the screen. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you notice the beans growing here? And the roads? Well, first of all, this does not appear to be the same house. But secondly, is it uncontestable, because that's what it says here, that the number 1 indicates the place where the house was hit and also the defect on the ground, the point where the rocket motors were recovered.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, would you let me read my report? You have it before you and I don't. So we are not quite in the same position.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Rocket motor parts were found. Can you see it? It says so above. It says: "122-millimetre grad rocket landed from the north and" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Let the witness read his report. Let's zoom out, yes. Where is it, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The investigators' opinion. It says so in Serbian. The investigators state that this projectile first hit the house at Aleksa Santica Street, number 50; went through the corner of the house; landed on the ground; the rocket motors separated; the projectile ricochetted and continued on its flight towards Bunicki Potok Street, number 233 and 231; rocket motor fragments of a 122-millimetre grad rocket were found or recovered on the scene; and the direction from which the projectile came was north, and we established it on the basis of the damage on the house.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's just let him read his report. Would you like to continue to read your comment below? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, but I was not given the opportunity to do so. I will read it, if you allow me. "According to available information, the projectile hit the ground" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You don't have to read out. You just read. We have it before us.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [In English] Okay. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, my question is this: First of all you claim that where you indicated, where you put the arrow, there was a crater, that's the point where these two men are standing?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, what I said was that the point of impact was some three metres from the front of the house, behind the opposite corner. And according to what the witnesses state here, and that is consistent with what I found, is that there was a water fountain there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And are you trying to say that the witnesses' words, 12 years later, are more reliable than an investigation, an on-site investigation, that was done at the time of the incident and that they actually failed to observe such a huge, such a big, defect on the ground in that yard?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karadzic, I -- they did not fail to observe anything. They said that two rocket motors were found in a crater 6.1 metre by 2.4 metres wide and 1.1 metre deep and several metal fragments in the crater, while the third motor was found in the yard close to the point of -- where the shell had hit the house.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And based on those two points, the damage on the house and the crater, they established where the north bearing is.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know how they established that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But you placed that point closer to the house and then you arrived at a different cardinal point and not the north; correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not make an error. The error could be half a metre at most, which does not affect the outcome.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Zecevic, do you deny that what the police capture there in the photo and indicated where the defect was on the ground, that that's where the shell landed on the ground?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. If you look at this photograph on the left-hand side, you can see those two people standing there in front of the house. You can also see, in front of them, some half -- some couple of metres from the corner of the house, you can see the crater. On the left-hand side we see the fence, but that is not the same part that you are referring to. In other words, my photograph and this photo that was taken by the investigator, who did not indicate the point of impact, they are very similar, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Would you please, then, with the assistance of the usher, use the pen and try to indicate the crater and draw a line between the damage on the house and the crater.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Could we zoom in a bit further on the left photo. Yes. Now, could you wait until assisted by our usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And why didn't you indicate the point where this fence was actually overturned?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that is a matter of choice or a decision, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, if the north -- if the bearing would remain to the north, could you tell us whose forces were to the north of Vogosca? To the north of Hrasnica. So if the police did establish where the north was and if we kept that same bearing for north, could you tell us whose forces were between that point and Vogosca?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, could you show me a military map and also the separation line? And then I could perhaps answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, it is the Defence case, Mr. Zecevic, that between Hrasnica and Vogosca there were only BH army troops. So if you draw a line to the north, between Hrasnica and Vogosca, there are no Serb forces along that line, in between there; "yes" or "no"? So what we have in between is Sokolovic Kolonija, Butmir, Dobrinja, Mojmilo, Novi Grad, Alipasino Polje, Prijevce [phoen], Hum, in other words, along that axis, all the way there to Vogosca, there are no Serb forces; correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't really answer that, Mr. Karadzic. Please show me a military map, show me the line -- the separation line, and then I can indicate it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we will do that time allowing, but what I'm trying to point out, Mr. Zecevic, is that the north bearing, there was a need to actually change that because there were no Serb forces in that direction; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's move on. You said today that this shell and this rocket-assisted projectile flew at the velocity of some 500 kilometres per hour?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The average velocity of such a projectile was some 150 to 170 metres per second.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter correction: 150 to 180 metres per second.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you investigate -- did you take part in the investigation of a shell landing -- this type of shell landing on the TV building in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Before we hear your evidence, answer, could you put your signature and the date of today on this picture. Today is 23rd of February.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will admit this as next Defence Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's Exhibit D1092, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And what was your next question? The shell landing on TV building in Sarajevo? Did you investigate? That was the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it correct that it was concluded that the shell ricochetted from the top, from the roof, of the building and then landed on a multi-storey building, ricochetted from there, and then detonated outside a wall in front of Studio C?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: Mr. President, just before we embark on what I suspect will be a lengthy cross-examination of the TV building incident, I'd like to note, as we previously noted, that the TV building incident has been removed from the indictment against the accused. We have redacted part of Dr. Zecevic's report which relates to the TV building incident. We simply want to make those observations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for the reminder. Think about your strategy, but it's time to take a five-minutes' break now, for the benefit of the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I might say right away, Your Excellency, it's not just about credibility. It's also about the link between this incident and another incident mentioned in the indictment. That is what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We are taking a five-minute break every half an hour to accommodate the witness's condition. Thank you. --- Break taken at 11.20 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, did you study this incident? Did you investigate this incident?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Me and two other colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you actually conduct an investigation at the time of the incident?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After the incident, not during the incident, obviously.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But not 12 years after. The same day or the next day, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please describe or confirm the following. The position taken by the investigative bodies was as follows: A projectile came in, ricochetted off the roof, and landed at the bottom of Studio C where it eventually exploded; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was a walkway along the wall facing the studio.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. How far was the place where the projectile ricochetted from the place of the actual explosion? Can you remember that, sir?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps between 10 and 15 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Our team was there, and they concluded that the distance was about 30 metres. Between the place where it ricochetted, you're quite right the explosion was somewhat nearer, but we put the figure at 50.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we get 1D13 -- 3319 in e-court, please. 1D3319.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's forget about the length. We wanted to make this slightly more feminine so we used the pink colour. Would this be a diagram that shows the disposition of the buildings there?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but I wasn't the person who produced this, so if you want me to address anything at all, you'll have to give me my findings to look at because my findings reflect this as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you have a diagram or a sketch of the physical buildings in your findings?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you're asking me to do this. This is something that I did 16 years ago. I'm telling you, give me the finding that I established at the time, and then I can comment on it. I came here straight from the prison. I have no documents on me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Can Mr. Gaynor please help us and then get that document for you. But you tell us whether the disposition of the buildings in terms of the diagram corresponds with your conclusions, generally speaking?

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: If I can interrupt at this point. I'm looking at the hard copies of the witness's report. But at page 129 in his language and 144 in the English language, there is a diagram in the witness's expert report relating to this incident. Now, that's been redacted from the version which has been uploaded to e-court, but I have a hard copy we can give to the witness now, if Your Honours wish.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have a copy for the benefit of the Defence team too? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAYNOR
utterances.text: The Defence already has a copy of this unredacted report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But in the meantime, can we go into private session briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. At page 126 of the document --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please -- is there a way we can get this in e-court, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We can get it put -- we can put it on the ELMO, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have that on the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have that in e-court, 1D3284, please, in e-court. As for this one, the page on which you showed a diagram of the buildings, e-court 1D3284. As for the ELMO, Mr. Zecevic, we can zoom in on that one, just keep it like this on the ELMO, your own diagram, please. The ELMO. [In English] May I ask the usher to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If necessary, you can skim through your report. In the meantime, we will upload in e-court.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Have I understood correctly that they are uploading the whole report, or what?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we upload 1D3284. In the meantime, Dr. Zecevic, you can take that report of yours, which is on the ELMO, you can read through them, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mm-hm. Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, we upload 1D3319.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: The participants "mesdo," means "site," site of ricochet, site of second ricochet, and site of explosion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So having refreshed your memory, please tell us whether you are in the position to answer any question or make any comments. This diagram is prepared by the Defence. I take it Mr. Karadzic is going to put his case or put questions to you, so let us know whether you can make any comments. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic? Or explain to Dr. Zecevic what this is about. And put your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll try to explain first. This is a diagram of the buildings, the walkway, Studio C, and the multi-storey building with the areas between the buildings. Let's forget about the 30- or 50- metre dilemma. Do you agree that the projectile ricochetted off the roof of this gangway, walkway building, it crossed this passage, it changed direction, and exploded just in front of Studio C; right?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But we can't forget about distance. The distance is material. My diagram and your diagram are very much alike but not identical.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. What about this passerelle Building, the walkway?

utterances.speaker: BERKO ZECEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I'm not going to do this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us see. First of all, I'd like to know how "mesdo" ricochet does -- I ask the interpreter: What does "mesdo rikoseta" mean?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The place where the projectile ricochetted.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you want me to explain, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I heard the explanation, thank you. What is your question, Mr. Karadzic? What do you want the witness to do?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want the witness to use this diagram, with these buildings, quite regardless of the distances, although he's free to draw the distances himself, to draw for us the trajectory of this projectile which ricochetted off the walkway building. And the second ricochet came from the multi-storeyed building until it eventually landed right in front of the Studio C wall.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, in my report, you have a clear and accurate diagram of the trajectory of the projectile, how it came in, how it ricochetted, and how it exploded on the ground right in front of the Studio C wall.
